Hi Sean,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we discussed, Aperture is moving forward with a private VPC deployment for our clinical document summarization pipeline. Before we commit to the PO we need a short written alignment on the sizing assumptions so our infra team can provision the networking and rack space.

Key constraints from our side:
- Burst windows are 08:00–10:00 and 18:00–20:00 PST, with a peak 95th-percentile QPS ~ 480 concurrent requests that map to ~1.8 tokens/sec per request for 1k token prompts.
- Maximum acceptable 99th pct latency for completion = 1.9s for p50/p95 within 220 tokens.
- Strict outbound egress cap to third-party storage: 4.5 TB/day.
- We want an initial reserve that handles a 1.6x surge for 6 months.

Can you put together a short operational profile (throughput numbers, warm-pool plan, fallback behavior) we can hand to our platform team? A simple table they can copy into their provisioning ticket would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Natalie

Natalie — attached is the short proposal and an operational profile you can paste into your provisioning ticket. High-level notes first:

Executive summary:
- Initial target sustained throughput: 480 concurrent requests (post-gateway) supporting mixed prompt sizes with 15% long-tail.
- Provision a dedicated pool of 12x A100-80GB-class GPUs (or equivalent ML-specific instances) in a single AZ to achieve baseline p95 completion latency < 1.7s at 220 tokens and acceptable headroom for the 1.6x surge.
- Warm-pool / pre-warming: reserve 2 standby nodes (20% capacity) always warm; scale +4 nodes in <90s when queue depth increases above threshold.
- Network: provision 25 Gbps egress per rack with QoS for priority model traffic; egress controls + token accounting to keep within 4.5 TB/day.

Sizing rationale (short):
- Benchmarks on the model family you mentioned indicate ~40 requests/sec per A100-80GB for 220-token interactive completion with our optimized runtime and batching enabled. With mixed prompt sizes and a 15% long tail multiplier, we assume effective per-GPU capacity ~32 r/s. 12 GPUs -> ~384 r/s (sustained), with continuous batching and prefix caching bringing effective concurrency to meet 480 concurrent requester load under expected service times.
- 1.6x surge headroom target: we recommend burst to 19 GPUs (adds ~7 GPUs) or enable short-term autoscale to 25 GPUs for extreme events (limited to 5 minutes bursts) — whichever matches your procurement constraints.

Operational controls and fallbacks:
- Canary routing: route 10% of traffic to a quantized model variant during peak windows to reduce per-token cost and absorb tail.
- Graceful degradation: when queue depth grows beyond 1.6x threshold, automatically switch 25% of low-priority background traffic to queuing (deferred processing) and issue 503 with ETA for latency-sensitive endpoints only as last resort.
- Cache warmup: run a scheduled prompt-set warmup job 15min before morning and evening peak windows to pre-fill KV cache and reduce cold-start penalty.

Attachments: 
- sean_private_pool_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal & one-page table)
- aperture_capacity_matrix.xlsx (their sample spreadsheet)

Action items for Aperture infra team (pasteable):
- Reserve rack space for 3 x 8U nodes (12 A100-sim GPUs) with 2 additional standby nodes and a network pipe >= 25 Gbps.
- Configure QoS for model egress; limit non-critical egress to 1 Gbps during peak windows.
- Add a simple health endpoint we can poll for KV cache readiness.

Cc'ing Kim and Lauren to confirm operational runbook items and to add any changes for SLA language.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk the infra team through the table tomorrow morning.

—Sean

Quick follow-up from infra/ops perspective — copying the high-priority checklist we want in the onboarding ticket:

1) Network and egress
- Confirm ASN peering and route advertisement window; schedule BGP test with network team.
- Ensure per-flow QoS for model priority traffic; mark control-plane traffic with DSCP 46.
- Enable egress metering at 30-minute buckets to avoid late-day spikes.

2) Autoscale policy stub
- Warm-pool baseline = 12 GPUs; add 4 GPUs when 5-min avg queue depth > 70% of available slots; further add up to 9 GPUs for extreme bursts, capped by manual approval at additional cost.

3) Observability and alerts
- p95 completion latency alert at 1.6s (warning) and 1.9s (critical).
- Cache-warm readiness metric.

4) Security/compliance
- Verify KMS key access pattern for inference keys; ensure logs are pushed to Aperture SIEM within 10s latency for audit window.

I'll drop these in the onboarding ticket and tag the network owner. Natalie — if that aligns, we can finalize the quote and delivery timeline (2–4 weeks post PO).

—Kim

Redwood Inference
